title: Grouped Data v1

findings.finding: Question 11 moves from constructing and reading grouped tables directly to reconstructing class frequencies from mixed cumulative statements.
findings.breakdown: Students must distinguish nested counts, subtract them to recover an interval frequency, and subtract two disjoint tails from the total. Earlier questions practise adding existing classes, but none separately rehearses these reconstruction decisions before they are combined.
findings.checked: Checked all teaching and the preceding practice, including p4-q2-c, p5-q5-b, p6-q8 and p7-q10. These establish totals and combined frequencies, but provide neither reconstruction bridge. Although Question 11 closes the exercise, the preceding questions do not build towards its combined demands.
findings.assumptions: Ordinary subtraction and totals are established. Calculator availability does not affect the reasoning demand.

repair.proposal: Immediately before Question 11, insert: (a) 'Of 50 people, 12 received 10 or fewer emails and 31 received 20 or fewer emails. How many received more than 10 but no more than 20 emails?' Answer: 19. (b) 'Of 50 people, 12 received 10 or fewer emails and 9 received more than 20 emails. How many received more than 10 but no more than 20 emails?' Answer: 29.

findings.doneWhen: Students separately practise subtracting nested counts and subtracting two disjoint tails before combining those decisions in Question 11.

findings.finding: The first histogram practice requires frequency polygons, but preceding teaching models only a histogram.
findings.breakdown: Students have no model for locating polygon points at class centres, joining them, retaining a zero-frequency class, or choosing the closing points.
findings.checked: The complete teaching contains no frequency-polygon construction. p8-information-block and p8-example-root explain class centres and histogram construction only. The completed practice graphs are answer-only and cannot supply preceding instruction.
findings.assumptions: General graph construction is prior knowledge; grouped frequency-polygon construction is not established by the supplied teaching. Calculator availability is immaterial.

repair.proposal: Extend p8-example-root by plotting (2,3), (7,7), (12,15), (17,19) and (22,6) on its histogram and joining consecutive points. Close the polygon at (-3,0) and (27,0), the centres of the adjacent outside classes. State that a zero-frequency class must still have a point at its centre with height zero.

findings.doneWhen: Before p9-q1-a, teaching shows how to choose the polygon points and closing points, including the treatment of a zero-frequency class.

findings.finding: Cumulative-frequency construction and its reversal are required without teaching the relationship between ordinary frequencies, cumulative totals and ogive points.
findings.breakdown: Students first need running totals and upper-boundary plotting in p10-q2. Later questions reuse that construction, and p23-q20-b requires reversing cumulative totals to recover class frequencies. The median teaching explains how to read a supplied ogive, rather than how to construct or reverse it.
findings.checked: Checked the complete teaching and intervening practice. p7-q11 requests reconstruction but supplies no instructional method. p8 models an ordinary histogram; p10 independently assigns cumulative construction. p12 models median reading only. Neither the earlier assignments nor their answer-only solutions supply the missing teaching.
findings.assumptions: Ordinary grouped histograms, addition and subtraction are established. Cumulative-frequency construction is a new variant here. Calculator availability is immaterial.

repair.proposal: Before p10-q2, reuse the p8 table. Model cumulative totals 3, 10, 25, 44, 50, explaining that each counts all observations through the current class. Draw cumulative bars with those heights and an ogive through (-0.5,0), (4.5,3), (9.5,10), (14.5,25), (19.5,44), (24.5,50). Explain that the points use upper class boundaries, rather than class centres, and that a zero-frequency class leaves the total unchanged. Add the reverse calculation: 'The frequency of 10–14 is 25−10=15: subtract the preceding cumulative total.'

findings.doneWhen: Before the first independent cumulative construction, students see running totals, cumulative bars, upper-boundary ogive points and recovery of an ordinary frequency by subtraction.

findings.finding: The topic explicitly builds on calculating a mean from an ungrouped frequency table, but does not rehearse that prior method.
findings.breakdown: The grouped-mean example requires weighting values by their frequencies and dividing by total frequency. Students who instead average the row values or divide by the number of classes have no opening review to expose that misunderstanding before class centres are introduced.
findings.checked: p11-mean-definition explicitly identifies the ungrouped frequency-table calculation as prior knowledge. Earlier teaching and the immediately preceding histogram exercise do not rehearse it. p8-review-block covers midpoints only. The grouped-mean definition supplies the new procedure but does not provide retrieval practice of the prior frequency-table method.
findings.assumptions: Ungrouped frequency-table means are prior knowledge, consistent with the stated course library. A calculator is assumed; numerical evaluation is not the missing review piece.

repair.proposal: Before p11-mean-definition, add three short review items: (a) 'Scores 2, 5, 8 have frequencies 3, 2, 1. How many scores are there?' Answer: 6. (b) 'For that table, find the total of all scores.' Answer: 24. (c) 'Scores 1, 4, 7 have frequencies 2, 1, 3. Find the mean.' Answer: 4.5. Keep the review within one page.

findings.doneWhen: The opening review rehearses weighting values and dividing by total frequency before applying that structure to class centres.

findings.finding: Graphical IQR is assigned without connecting the quartiles to cumulative-frequency heights.
findings.breakdown: The median example demonstrates the 50% position only. Students receive no explicit connection from the lower and upper quartiles to N/4 and 3N/4 on the cumulative-frequency axis before being asked to read and subtract their score values.
findings.checked: Checked all preceding teaching and practice. p12-teaching and p12-example-demonstration establish median reading, but no preceding prompt models or cues either graphical quartile position. Prior knowledge of quartiles and IQR does not itself establish their use on the newly introduced cumulative graph.
findings.assumptions: Quartiles and IQR are prior knowledge from the separately taught Quartiles and Box Plots content. The missing component is applying them to cumulative-frequency graphs. Calculator availability is immaterial.

repair.proposal: Before p18-q11, add: 'For an ogive with total frequency N, locate Q1 at cumulative frequency N/4 and Q3 at cumulative frequency 3N/4. Read their score values using horizontal then vertical guides, as for the median. Estimate IQR = Q3 − Q1.'

findings.doneWhen: Students receive the cumulative-frequency positions and reading route for both quartiles before independently estimating graphical IQR.

protectedGroups.observation: Comparing two representations of the same observations exposes which information grouping removes.
protectedGroups.varies: Individual-value rows versus three-value class intervals.

protectedGroups.observation: Students must attend to which endpoint is included rather than assuming one fixed convention.
protectedGroups.varies: The placement of strict and inclusive inequality signs.
protectedGroups.invariant: A compound inequality describing one interval.

protectedGroups.observation: Doubling every frequency preserves the estimated mean; doubling class values doubles it; reversing the frequency distribution changes its location.
protectedGroups.varies: First the common frequency multiplier, then the class scale, then the allocation of frequencies.
protectedGroups.invariant: The weighted-mean method and, within each adjacent comparison, the remaining table features.

protectedGroups.observation: Changing the frequency of a class centred at the current estimated mean preserves that mean, including when the frequency becomes zero.
protectedGroups.varies: Only the frequency of the class centred at 50.
protectedGroups.invariant: All classes, other frequencies and estimated mean.

protectedGroups.observation: Adding one to every class endpoint adds one to the estimated mean.
protectedGroups.varies: Every class endpoint increases by one.

protectedGroups.observation: Changing the grouping changes representative centres and can preserve or alter the estimated mean.
protectedGroups.varies: Splitting or merging the upper classes.
protectedGroups.invariant: Total frequency and the first two occupied classes.
